title: Trichome Development, Maturity Heterogeneity and Harvest Evidence

content.overview: Glandular trichomes develop and mature over time, but they do not all reach the same stage together. Genotype, plant age, bract surface and flower position contribute to heterogeneity, so maturity decisions require representative evidence.

vocabulary.definition: Glandular trichome type with a secretory head associated with cannabinoid and terpene production.
Condition where structures within the same plant or tissue population are at different developmental stages at the same time.
Opening or structural breakdown that can occur in mature/senescing glandular heads.

sections.title: Trichome type and morphology change during flowering
sections.body: Cannabis studies have documented sessile and stalked capitate trichomes, changing stalk/head characteristics and resin morphology over flower development.

sections.title: Genotype and age matter
sections.body: Capitate trichome number, development and degree of maturation differed between studied genotypes and across plant ages.

sections.title: Color is evidence, not a universal threshold
sections.body: Clear/cloudy/amber appearance can accompany maturation, but asynchronous development means no single color percentage is a universal harvest rule. Use representative sampling and production goals.

workedExamples: A microscope view dominated by amber heads on one exposed bract does not prove interior flowers share the same maturity distribution.
Two genotypes at the same flower week can show different trichome morphology and maturation.
commonMistakes: Using an internet color percentage as a universal rule.
Ignoring post-harvest handling effects on trichome morphology.
content.practicalApplication: Define repeatable sample positions across several plants/flowers and record trichome distribution with broader flower-development and quality criteria.
content.summary: Maturity is a distribution across a biological population, not a single trichome color reading.
